French Automotive Exports Edge Up in Second Quarter as Domestic Sales Hold Steady

France’s automotive sector reported modest growth in exports during the second quarter of 2024, with domestic sales maintaining a stable trajectory, according to data released Thursday by the National Automotive Federation (FNA). The figures underscore a period of steady performance for one of the country’s key industrial sectors amid a stable macroeconomic backdrop.

Total vehicle exports rose 2.1% year-on-year to 334,000 units between April and June, driven in part by sustained demand from European neighbors and North Africa. Passenger cars accounted for the largest share, while commercial vehicle shipments also saw incremental gains. “We’re seeing resilience in export demand, particularly for compact and hybrid models,” said FNA president Lucien Marchand. “Our members are benefiting from established trade relationships and ongoing consumer interest in efficient vehicles.”

Domestically, registrations of new vehicles reached 480,000 units in the quarter, holding broadly steady compared to the same period last year. Industry analysts attributed this stability to continued consumer incentives for low-emission vehicles and a gradual recovery in household purchasing power. “Consumer confidence is supporting demand, especially for newer electric and hybrid models,” commented Sylvie Girard, an automotive analyst at Banque du Midi.

Auto parts exports also reflected the sector’s positive momentum, rising 1.5% year-on-year. The French Ministry of Industry noted that component demand from Italy and Spain remained strong.

The FNA said it expects moderate growth to continue through the rest of the year. “We anticipate a steady environment for French automotive activity, with no major disruptions on the horizon,” Marchand added.
